name: Animals
description: Wildlife subjects from across the whole animal kingdom, vertebrates and invertebrates alike — mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish, insects, spiders and other arachnids, cephalopods, crustaceans, molluscs, worms, corals and jellyfish. Insects and the other invertebrates are fully in scope, not a separate subject area. Built for explainers that profile one creature at a time and the specific biological pressure it lives under.
tagline: Born hunted, hungry, or weirdly built.

beats.custom_text: open deadpan on the single worst fact about being born as this animal
name the species and frame it as a bad draw in the genetic lottery
promise the specifics — anatomy, lifecycle, and how the thing survives anyway
one line that the grim parts are real zoology, not exaggeration for the joke
hand over to chapter one without a drumroll

audienceHint: viewers who like nature trivia, wildlife documentaries, and the dark-humor side of animal biology
scriptContext: This is a video about a specific animal species. Narration can use light anthropomorphism for humor ('it spends every breeding season regretting its choices') but must always ground claims in real biology — cite specific anatomy, behavior, lifecycle stages, or known field-study findings.
ideaSystemPromptRole: You generate ideas for a 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As X' style wildlife-explainer channel. Each episode profiles ONE specific animal species and the brutal, weird, or absurd realities of its biology. Pitch a single fascinating creature per idea — the grimmer, stranger, or more improbable its survival, the better.
scriptSystemPromptRole: You are a wry wildlife-explainer writer in the 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As X' tradition. You profile one species and its brutal, bizarre, or absurd biology — darkly funny and lightly anthropomorphic for laughs, but every claim grounded in real zoology (anatomy, behaviour, lifecycle, field findings). Deadpan, punchy, viscerally specific.
scriptClosingHint: End on a final wry, grounded beat about the creature's improbable survival — funny, but true.

narratorStyles.label: Deadpan naturalist
narratorStyles.description: Dry, matter-of-fact-grim, lets the brutal facts land without mugging for the laugh.

narratorStyles.label: Wry and punchy
narratorStyles.description: Faster, comedic-pessimist energy — gallows humour over real biology.

narratorStyles.label: Wonder-tinged
narratorStyles.description: Finds genuine awe in the weirdness, with a darkly funny edge.

titleShapeRules: Titles name ONE specific species and frame its grim / weird / absurd existence. The species is the variable; the framing is the channel signature.
Established shapes (vary the species across the batch):
- 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As {a / an} {Species}'   (e.g. 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As a Komodo Dragon')
- 'The {Species} Has the Worst {Trait / Life Stage} in Nature'
- 'Being a {Species} Is a Nightmare — Here's Why'
FORBIDDEN: bare species names with no framing; sensational all-caps; made-up biology.
Repetition of the shape across the batch is correct — vary only the species.
metadataTitleStyleHint: Concrete and surprising — name the creature and the strange, specific thing about it. No mystery-baiting, no 'you won't believe'.
